title: Exact operator dynamics in Lindbladian Wess-Zumino-Witten conformal field theories
authors: Qicheng Tang, Ruhanshi Barad, Xueda Wen
abstract: Understanding the time evolution of physical observables in open quantum many-body systems coupled to external environments is a natural and difficult problem, and exact results are still rare. In this work, we study this problem for Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) conformal field theories with Lindblad jump operators linear in Kac-Moody current modes. We investigate the exact operator dynamics generated by these Lindbladians, identifying classes of current operators whose Heisenberg equations close and can therefore be solved analytically using the underlying current algebra. In Abelian $U(1)_k$ WZW theories, this closure of operator dynamics holds for arbitrary settings of jump rates and includes exactly tractable cooling dynamics. In contrast, for non-Abelian WZW theories, exact closure occurs only for symmetric current-mode dissipation, where upward and downward current-mode transitions occur with equal rates, and even then it leads to a simple closed evolution only for a single current operator. Generic imbalances, including those needed for cooling, produce additional non-Abelian terms and prevent closure of the opeartor dynamics. Consequently, the current algebra gives rise to a broad family of exactly solvable dissipative dynamics in the Abelian setting, whereas in the non-Abelian case it singles out only a special exactly solvable dynamics corresponding to an infinite-temperature bath.
summary: The paper investigates the time evolution of observables in WZW CFTs subjected to environmental coupling via a Lindbladian. It finds that while Abelian models allow for broad classes of exactly solvable dissipative dynamics, non-Abelian structures severely restrict solvability, requiring high degrees of symmetry in dissipation rates to maintain algebraic closure.
main_problem: The central problem is determining the exact time evolution of physical observables in open quantum many-body systems coupled to environments, specifically within Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW) conformal field theories.
main_result: Exact solvability for operator dynamics is highly restricted: it holds generally in the Abelian $U(1)_k$ case but requires specific symmetries (like symmetric dissipation rates) in the non-Abelian setting, leading to a loss of general algebraic closure.
method: The authors analyze the Lindbladian master equation by checking for the closure of the Heisenberg equations of motion for current operators and their products, rather than solving the full Liouvillian spectrum.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using WZW CFTs whose dynamics are governed by a Lindblad master equation. The Hamiltonian is derived from the Sugawara construction, involving affine Kac-Moody currents ($J^b_p$).
key_observables: Operator dynamics (e.g., $\langle J^p J^r angle(t)$), closure of Heisenberg equations for current modes, and mixing time ($	au_{mix}$).
important_parameters: The level $k$ of the WZW theory, the structure constants of the underlying Lie algebra ($g$), and the specific rates/symmetries of the Lindblad jump operators ($\gamma$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often focuses on chiral holomorphic sectors or assumes initial states are Gaussian to simplify expectation value calculations. The closure of the Heisenberg equation is a necessary but not sufficient condition for full solvability.
figures_summary: Not specified in the notes, but the structure implies comparisons between Abelian and non-Abelian dynamics under dissipation.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the problem by first establishing the general framework (WZW models and Lindbladians), then contrasting the solvable Abelian case ($U(1)_k$) with the constrained non-Abelian case ($SU(2)_k$), culminating in a discussion of necessary symmetry conditions for exact solvability.
why_interesting: This work provides deep insights into how algebraic structures (like current algebras) constrain the dynamics of open quantum systems, offering powerful theoretical tools applicable to understanding dissipation and thermalization in complex field theories.
